briefdescription.para: ESC character — used as a standalone escape or as the Alt prefix.

CSI modifier prefix: ESC [ 1 ; — used when a modifier is active.

detaileddescription.para: The 1 is the parameter position for the key number (always 1 for cursor and F1–F4 keys); the modifier code N follows the semicolon.

Base value for the modifier parameter when no modifiers are held.

detaileddescription.para: The xterm modifier parameter is 1 + shift + alt + ctrl. When the result equals noModifier (1), the parameter is omitted from the sequence.

briefdescription.para: Maps simple keys to their fixed single-byte sequences.

detaileddescription.para: These keys always produce the same output regardless of modifier state. Handled before cursor/function/editing keys in mapPlain().

briefdescription.para: Maps Ctrl+punctuation key codes to their control-character sequences.

detaileddescription.para: These supplement the Ctrl+A…Z range handled inline in mapCtrl().

briefdescription.para: Progressive keyboard protocol flag: disambiguate escape codes (bit 0).
Progressive keyboard protocol flag: report all keys as escape codes (bit 3).
Maps JUCE simple key codes to their CSI u key numbers.

briefdescription.para: Converts a JUCE KeyPress into an xterm escape sequence string.

detaileddescription.para:
Dispatches to the appropriate private handler based on which modifier keys are active:
Ctrl-only → mapCtrl()
Alt (with or without Shift/Ctrl) → mapAlt()
No modifier (or Shift-only) → mapPlain()

parameterdescription.para: The JUCE key event to translate.
When true, cursor keys use SS3 sequences (\x1bOA) instead of CSI sequences (\x1b[A), matching xterm's "application cursor keys" mode (DECCKM, \x1b[?1h).
Progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) flags from the active screen. 0 = legacy mode (no enhanced encoding). Bit 0 (1): disambiguate escape codes. Bit 3 (8): report all keys as escape codes.

simplesect.para: The escape sequence as a juce::String, or an empty string if the key has no defined mapping (caller should ignore the event).

briefdescription.para: Handles Ctrl+key combinations (without Alt).

detaileddescription.para:
Produces control characters and a small set of special sequences:
Ctrl+A…Z → bytes 0x01…0x1A
Ctrl+@ or Ctrl+Space → NUL (0x00)
Ctrl+[ → ESC (0x1B), Ctrl+\ → FS (0x1C), Ctrl+] → GS (0x1D), Ctrl+^ → RS (0x1E), Ctrl+_ → US (0x1F)

When progressive keyboard protocol flag 1 (disambiguate) or flag 8 (all keys) is active, Ctrl+key combinations produce CSI u sequences instead of legacy control characters, using the lowercase codepoint as the key number (e.g. Ctrl+C → CSI 99;5u).

parameterdescription.para: The raw JUCE key code (from KeyPress::getKeyCode()).
Full modifier state (Ctrl is always set; Shift may be).
Progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) flags.

simplesect.para: The control-character sequence or CSI u sequence, or an empty string if code has no Ctrl mapping.

memberdef.name: mapAlt

briefdescription.para: Handles Alt+key combinations.

detaileddescription.para: Strips Alt from the modifier set, recursively calls map() to obtain the base sequence, then prepends ESC (\x1b). If the key has no special sequence but carries a printable character, that character is ESC-prefixed instead (standard "meta key" behaviour).
Shift and Ctrl are forwarded to the inner map() call so that combinations like Alt+Shift+F1 are encoded correctly.

parameterdescription.para: Raw JUCE key code.
Full modifier state (including Alt).
Text character associated with the key event.
Forwarded to the inner map() call.
Progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) flags (forwarded to inner map() call).

simplesect.para: ESC-prefixed sequence, or an empty string if neither a special sequence nor a printable character is available.

memberdef.name: mapPlain

briefdescription.para: Handles unmodified keys (and Shift-only combinations).

detaileddescription.para:
Dispatches to the appropriate sub-handler in priority order:
simpleKeys table — Return, Backspace, Tab, Escape.
cursorKeys table — arrow keys, routed through cursorKey().
F1–F12 range — routed through functionKey().
Home, End, and editing cluster — routed through editingKey().
Printable character fallback — passes the text character through as-is.

parameterdescription.para: Raw JUCE key code.
Modifier state (Shift may be set; Ctrl/Alt are not).
Text character associated with the key event.
Forwarded to cursorKey().
Progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) flags.

simplesect.para: The escape sequence or character string, or empty if unmapped.

briefdescription.para: Computes the xterm modifier parameter for a given modifier state.

detaileddescription.para: The parameter is defined as: N=1+(shift?1:0)+(alt?2:0)+(ctrl?4:0)+(meta?8:0)

The Super/Meta kitty bit is applied only on macOS, where isCommandDown() reflects the physical Cmd key (Super/Meta-equivalent, distinct from Ctrl). On Windows and Linux, JUCE aliases commandModifier to ctrlModifier, so isCommandDown() returns the same value as isCtrlDown(). Adding that bit there would double-count Ctrl (producing modifier 13 instead of 5 for a plain Ctrl+key), which terminals and editors do not recognise as Ctrl. When N == 1 (no modifiers active), callers omit the modifier parameter from the sequence entirely.

parameterdescription.para: The modifier key state to encode.

simplesect.para: Integer modifier code in the range [1, 16].
This function is noexcept and performs no allocation.

parameterdescription.para: The Unicode key number (e.g. 13 for Enter).
Active modifier keys.

memberdef.name: shouldUseCsiU

briefdescription.para: Determines whether a simple key should use CSI u encoding.

detaileddescription.para:
Applies the progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) rules:
Legacy (flags=0): never CSI u.
Disambiguate (flag 1): Escape always gets CSI u. Enter/Tab/Backspace get CSI u only when a non-lock modifier (Shift/Ctrl/Alt) is held; unmodified presses stay legacy so the user can still type reset after a crash.
All keys (flag 8): all simple keys get CSI u unconditionally.

parameterdescription.para: JUCE key code.
Active modifier keys.
Progressive keyboard protocol (CSI u) flags.

simplesect.para: true if the key should be encoded as CSI u.

briefdescription.para: Tests whether a key code is an ASCII text key.

detaileddescription.para: Text keys are the set of keys that produce printable ASCII characters in the CSI u protocol spec: a-z (JUCE codes A-Z), 0-9, and the punctuation keys: (backtick) - = [ ] \ ; ' , . / and space.

parameterdescription.para: JUCE key code.

simplesect.para: true if the key is an ASCII text key.

briefdescription.para: Builds the escape sequence for an arrow key press.

detaileddescription.para:
Without modifiers:
Normal cursor mode: CSI <final> (e.g. \x1b[A)
Application cursor mode: SS3 <final> (e.g. \x1bOA)
With modifiers: always CSI 1 ; N <final> regardless of cursor mode (e.g. Shift+Up: \x1b[1;2A).

parameterdescription.para: The letter identifying the direction: A/B/C/D.
Active modifier keys.
When true and no modifiers are active, use SS3 prefix instead of CSI.

briefdescription.para: Builds the escape sequence for a function key press (F1–F12).

detaileddescription.para: F1–F4 use SS3 sequences; F5–F12 use CSI tilde sequences. The xterm numeric codes for F5–F12 skip values 16 and 22 (historical gaps):

parameterdescription.para: JUCE key code in the range [F1Key, F12Key].
Active modifier keys.

simplesect.para: The complete escape sequence string, or empty if juceKey is outside the F1–F12 range.

briefdescription.para: Builds the escape sequence for an editing-cluster key press.

detaileddescription.para: Handles Home, End, Insert, Delete, Page Up, and Page Down.

listitem.para: Home / End: CSI H / CSI F, or CSI 1 ; N H / CSI 1 ; N F with mods.
Insert / Delete / PgUp / PgDn: CSI <code> ~, or CSI <code> ; N ~ with mods.

parameterdescription.para: JUCE key code for one of the editing-cluster keys.
Active modifier keys.

briefdescription.para: Namespace-struct providing static key-mapping utilities.

detaileddescription.para: All members are static; this struct is never instantiated. It acts as a scoped namespace with private implementation details hidden from callers.
The single public entry point is map(). All other methods are private helpers that handle specific modifier combinations or key families.
